## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
All measured points start at N=4000, already past the L1d spill at N≈949, so the L1d→L2 transition is not directly observed. At q=0.01, cost FALLS from 8.753 ns/p at N=4000 to 7.959 at N=262000 — overhead amortization at small N, not a cache effect. The L2 spill at N≈60787 falls between N=16000 and N=65000; crossing it, cost stays FLAT (8.081 → 7.985 ns/p), with no knee at L2→DRAM. Death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape: at q=0.25 the curve is flat at ~10.2 ns/p from N=65000 onward, versus ~8.0 at q=0.01. The large-N plateau is independent of cache level, indicating the kernel is not streaming-limited.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.67 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 34.4% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The cell is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: ns/p is flat across N at all death rates, and bandwidth never approaches the ceiling in any regime. Death rate degrades the floor: q=0.05 holds ~8.3 GB/s through N=262000 then falls to 7.81 at N≥1M; q=0.25 collapses to 6.74 GB/s (26.7% of ceiling) and stays there. The transition is driven by churn, not by N — branchy respawn cost rises with death rate and dominates by q=0.25.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within a single particle, not across particles. `fmul.4s v7, v18, v3` and `fadd.4s v7, v16, v7` operate on four floats from one particle's position/velocity. `ldr q16, [x11]` loads 16 bytes, `ext.16b v18, v16, v17, #0xc` rearranges the AoS layout, and `ld1.s {v17}[1], [x12]` is a gather — an indexed NEON load inserting one element. Stores are `str q7, [x11]` (16 bytes) and `strb w11, [x10], #0x1` for the death flag. The per-particle stride is 0x44 (68 bytes). Component-wise vec on a 68-byte working set explains the low bandwidth: each particle does modest compute on a small footprint, so the kernel is compute/overhead-bound. The byte-granular `strb` death-flag stores and the heavily branchy respawn path (`cbz`, 35 `bl` calls to `_layouts.L1.data.Data.spawn`) cap throughput further as churn rises.

## Verdict
Refuted — the cell peaks at 8.67 GB/s, only 34% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling, with no regime approaching streaming. Component-wise auto-vectorization within particles (`fmul.4s`, `ld1.s` gather) produces a compute-bound kernel whose ns/p is flat across N (7.96–8.05 at q=0.01), and death rate raises the floor to 10.2 ns/p at q=0.25, dropping bandwidth to 6.74 GB/s. The hypothesis that auto-vectorization approaches the streaming ceiling does not hold in any measured regime.
